To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
finite blocklength coding is necessary for distributed transmission of independent messages over interference channels with feedback.

the optimal performance of the distributed terminals in a channel with feedback is not achievable by coded transmission with large effective length codes, but is achievable by coded transmission using finite blocklength codes.
the optimal transmission strategy for distributed communication over channels with feedback is a coded transmission scheme using finite effective length block codes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: what is the role of finite blocklength coding in the distributed transmission of independent messages over channels with feedback?
the design of finite effective length codes that preserve correlation between inputs of the terminals and hence achieve optimality.
the design of codes for the interference channel with feedback that can achieve optimal rates with finite effective length.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimal transmission strategy in the interference channel with feedback is to use finite effective length codes.
finite effective length coding is necessary for optimality in the interference channel with feedback.
the use of finite effective length codes in a communication system with feedback and independent messages is necessary to achieve the capacity region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of feedback in communication systems with distributed terminals necessitates finite blocklength codes.
finite blocklength coding is necessary for optimality in the presence of feedback, and that this necessity is a consequence of the correlation between the input symbols at the terminals.
, for interference channels with feedback, coded transmission using finite-length codes with optimal effective length is necessary for achieving optimality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
finite blocklength coding strategies are necessary to achieve optimally for distributed communication over channels with feedback.
the presence of feedback in a communication system necessitates the use of finite effective length codes to achieve optimality in terms of the rate region.
the use of feedback at the transmitter side can be beneficial even when the channel has no feedback.
